name: Alert Type
description: Naarni-managed catalog of telemetry alerts. Fill it in top to bottom like a short form — name it, choose what to watch, say when it should trigger, then how it looks and where it goes. No technical ID needed; one is generated for you.

fields.label: Step 1 · Name this alert
fields.description: Give the alert a clear name your team will recognise, and how serious it is.

fields.label: Alert Name
fields.description: Plain-English name, e.g. 'Battery Pack Overheating' or 'Vehicle Speeding'.

fields.label: How serious is it?
fields.description: Warning 🟠 = keep an eye on it. Critical 🔴 = needs action now.

fields.label: Available to customers
fields.description: When unchecked, this alert is hidden from the customer catalog.

fields.label: Step 2 · What to watch
fields.description: Pick the reading coming off the vehicle that this alert should look at.

fields.label: Vehicle reading to watch
fields.description: Optional. Leave blank to define this alert from the Conditions table only (AND/OR).

fields.label: Kind of reading
fields.description: Filled in automatically. Number = compare against a value. Category/Yes-No = match a specific state.

fields.label: Unit
fields.description: Shown next to the value, e.g. °C, km/h, %, V. Filled in automatically; you can adjust it.

fields.label: Step 3 · When should it trigger?
fields.description: Choose the condition. Read it as a sentence: “Trigger when <reading> <condition> <value>”.

fields.label: Trigger when the value is…
fields.options:
is greater than (>)
is greater than or equal to (≥)
is less than (<)
is less than or equal to (≤)
is exactly (=)
is not (≠)
fields.description: How to compare the live reading against your value below.

fields.label: …this number
fields.description: For number readings only. Example: for 'speeding', greater than 80.

fields.label: …this value
fields.description: For category / Yes-No readings. Pick from the list of allowed values.

fields.options:
Choosing the condition
is greater than (>) — fires when the reading goes above your number. Use for speed, temperature, voltage.
is less than (<) — fires when it drops below your number. Use for low battery %, low pressure.
≥ / ≤ — same, but also fires exactly at the number.
is exactly (=) — fires when the state matches, e.g. connectivity is exactly OFFLINE.
is not (≠) — fires when the state is anything other than the value.

fields.label: Preview
fields.options: Fill in the steps above to see a preview of when this alert fires.

fields.label: Step 3b · More conditions (optional)
fields.description: Combine several readings. Conditions in the SAME group must all be true together (AND); different groups are alternatives (OR). The alert fires when any one group fully matches. Leave empty for a single-condition alert. Example: Group 1 = motor temp > 80 AND speed > 5; Group 2 = coolant < 10  →  fires on either situation.

fields.label: Trigger Expression
fields.options: Add conditions above to see the full trigger expression.

fields.label: Step 4 · How it looks & where it goes
fields.description: Make the notification clear, and choose which Teams channel it posts to. Vehicle number and position are always included automatically.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Emoji shown on the notification. Leave blank to use the severity default (🔴 critical / 🟠 warning).

fields.label: Display Title
fields.description: Headline shown on the notification. Leave blank to use the Alert Name.

fields.label: Readings to show in the alert
fields.description: Pick the readings the service engineer should see. They appear in the alert (and on Teams) as 'Label = Value', e.g. Motor Temperature = 142, Battery SOC = 15%. The reading(s) the alert triggers on are always included automatically.

fields.label: Readings to Show
fields.description: Type to search and select one or more readings.

fields.label: Custom Message (optional)
fields.description: Leave blank — by default the alert shows the readings above as 'Label = Value'. To override, write your own line using {curly} placeholders: {vehicle} {registration} {parameter} {value} {unit} {op} {limit} {location} {time} {details} {condition}, or a reading's own token e.g. {p_bat_soc}.

fields.label: Internal Notes
fields.description: Optional notes for Naarni staff. Not shown to customers.
